questions.q: In the interim government formed in 1946, the Vice-President of the Executive Council was: [1995]
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru was the Vice-President of the Executive Council in the Interim Government of 1946. Other members like C. Rajagopalachari headed Education and Dr. Rajendra Prasad headed Food & Agriculture.

questions.q: Hooghly was used as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal by: [1995]
questions.e: The Portuguese used Hooghly as a base for piracy in the Bay of Bengal until they were finally subdued by Qasim Khan, the governor of Bengal during Shah Jahan's reign in 1631-32.

questions.q: The 'Modi script' was employed in the documents of the: [1995]
questions.e: The Modi script was employed in the documents of the Marathas. It was mainly used for maintaining revenue and administrative records during their rule.

questions.q: Examine the map given below: The places marked 1, 2, 3 and 4 were respectively the seats of powers of the: [1995]
questions.e: Based on the historical map of Maratha confederacy seats: 1 represents Scindias (Gwalior), 2 represents Holkars (Indore), 3 represents Gaekwads (Baroda), and 4 represents Bhonsles (Nagpur).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched? [1995]
o: Battle of Buxar-Mir Jafar vs. Clive
Battle of Kharda-Nizam vs. East India Company
Battle of Wandiwash-French vs. East India Company
questions.e: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) saw the French finally defeated by the English. The Battle of Buxar (1764) involved Munro defeating a combined force of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-daula, and Shah Alam II.

questions.q: The word Adivasi was used for the first time to refer to the tribal people by: [1995]
questions.e: Thakkar Bappa used the word 'Adivasi' for the first time to refer to tribal people. The term 'Adivasi' literally means primitive people or original inhabitants.

questions.q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer: List I: (A) Governor-General of Presidency of Fort William (1773) (B) Governor-General of India (1833) (C) Governor-General and Viceroy (1858) (D) Governor-General and Crown Representative (1935). List II: 1️⃣ Archibald Percival Wavell 2️⃣ James Andrew Broun-Ramsay 3️⃣ Charles Cornwallis 4️⃣ Gilbert John Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound 5️⃣ Louis Mountbatten. [1996]
questions.e: Lord Cornwallis served as Governor-General of Bengal (Fort William). Lord Dalhousie was Governor-General of India (1848-56). Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and first Governor-General of independent India. Lord Wavell served from 1943-1947.

questions.q: "His principal forte was social and religious reform. He relied upon legislation to do away with social ills and work unceasingly for the eradication of child marriage and the purdah system. To encourage consideration of social problems on a national scale, he inaugurated the Indian National Social Conference..." The reference in this passage is to: [1996]
questions.e: Mahadev Govind Ranade was a distinguished scholar and social reformer who worked for women's rights and inaugurated the Indian National Social Conference, which met alongside the Congress sessions.

questions.q: The following advertisement: "THE MARVEL OF THE CENTURY, THE WONDER OF THE WORLD... BY MESSERS LUMIERE BROTHERS... AT WATSON'S HOTEL TONIGHT" appeared in the Times of India dated 7th August: [1996]
questions.e: This was the first advertisement for Indian cinema, specifically the Lumiere Brothers' Cinematograph, appearing in the Times of India on August 7, 1896.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first European to initiate the policy of taking part in the quarrels of Indian princes with a view to acquire territories? [1996]
questions.e: Dupleix, the French governor of Pondicherry, initiated the policy of intervening in the quarrels of Indian princes to acquire territories for France and trained native sepoys for this purpose.

questions.q: Consider the following landmarks in Indian education: 1️⃣ Hindu College, Calcutta 2️⃣ University of Calcutta 3️⃣ Adam's Report 4️⃣ Wood's Despatch. The correct chronological order of these landmarks is: [1996]
questions.e: Hindu College, Calcutta was founded in 1817. Adam's Report was submitted between 1835-38. Wood's Despatch came in 1854, and the University of Calcutta was established in 1858.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an important historical novel written during the latter half of the nineteenth century? [1996]
questions.e: Durgesh Nandini was a historical novel written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee between 1862 and 1864 in the Bengali language.

questions.q: Who among the following was associated with suppression of thugs? [1997]
questions.e: Captain William Sleeman was appointed by Governor-General Lord William Bentinck to lead the efforts to suppress the Thugs in India.

questions.q: What is the correct chronological sequence of the following? 1️⃣ Wood's Education Despatch 2️⃣ Macaulay's minute on education 3️⃣ The Sargent Education Report 4️⃣ Indian Education (Hunter Commission). Select the correct answer using the code given below: [1997]
questions.e: Macaulay's Minute on Education was in 1835. Wood's Despatch was in 1854. The Hunter Commission was in 1882-83, and the Sargent Education Report was in 1944.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer: List-I: (A) Moplah revolt (B) Pabna revolt (C) Eka movement (D) Birsa Munda revolt. List-II: 1️⃣ Kerala 2️⃣ Bihar 3️⃣ Bengal 4️⃣ Awadh. [1997]
questions.e: The Moplah revolt (1921) occurred in Kerala. The Pabna revolt (1873) was in East Bengal. The Eka movement (1921-22) was in Awadh (UP). The Birsa Munda revolt (1899) took place in Ranchi, Bihar (now Jharkhand).

questions.q: The educated middle class in India: [1998]
o: remained neutral to the revolt of 1857
questions.e: The modern educated Indians, along with the middle and upper classes, did not support the 1857 revolt. The revolt was largely restricted to certain areas and lacked the support of many Indian sections.

questions.q: The paintings of Abanindranath Tagore are classified as: [1999]
questions.e: Abanindranath Tagore is recognized as the leader of the Revivalist Movement in modern Indian painting, particularly the Bengal School of Art.

questions.q: There was no independent development of industries in India during British rule because of the: [1999]
o: preference of the rich to invest in land
questions.e: British economic policy treated India as a source of raw materials and a market for finished goods. Consequently, the wealthy in India preferred to invest in land rather than independent industrial ventures.

questions.q: The first feature film (talkie) to be produced in India was: [1999]
questions.e: Alam Ara, directed by Ardeshir Irani, was the first Indian sound film (talkie). It was so popular that police were needed to control the crowds.

questions.q: The Governor-General who followed a spirited "Forward" policy towards Afghanistan was: [1999]
questions.e: Lord Lytton (1876-80) was the Governor-General who pursued the "Forward Policy" towards Afghanistan, leading to the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

questions.q: At a time when empires in Europe were crumbling before the might of Napoleon, which one of the following Governors-General kept the British flag flying high in India? [1999]
questions.e: During the Napoleonic era, Lord Wellesley expanded British influence in India through the Subsidiary Alliance system, effectively keeping the British flag flying high amidst European instability.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct? 1️⃣ 'Neel Darpan' was a play based on the exploitation of the Indigo farmers. 2️⃣ The author of the play 'Ghashiram Kotwal' is Vijay Tendulkar. 3️⃣ The play 'Navann' by Nabin Chandra Das was based on the famine of Bengal. 4️⃣ Urdu theatre used to depend heavily on Parsi theatre. [1999]
questions.e: While Neel Darpan (Dinabandhu Mitra) and Ghashiram Kotwal (Vijay Tendulkar) are correctly described, the statement about 'Navann' is often questioned or attributed differently in literature; however, Neel Darpan was indeed essential to the Indigo revolt.

questions.q: Match List-I (Books) with List-II (Authors) and select the correct answer: (A) The First Indian War of Independence (B) Anand Math (C) Life Divine (D) Sadhana. List-II: 1️⃣ Rabindranath Tagore 2️⃣ Sri Aurobindo 3️⃣ Bankim Chandra Chatterji 4️⃣ Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. [1999]
questions.e: V.D. Savarkar wrote 'The First Indian War of Independence'. Bankim Chandra Chatterji wrote 'Anand Math'. Sri Aurobindo wrote 'Life Divine', and Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Sadhana'.

questions.q: Consider the following events: 1️⃣ Indigo Revolt 2️⃣ Santhal Rebellion 3️⃣ Deccan Riot 4️⃣ Mutiny of the Sepoys. The correct chronological sequence of these events is: [1999]
questions.e: The Santhal Rebellion occurred in 1855-56. The Mutiny of Sepoys (Revolt) was in 1857. The Indigo Revolt took place in 1860, and the Deccan Riots were in 1875.

questions.q: Match List-I (Year) with List-II (Event) and select the correct answer: (A) 1775 (B) 1780 (C) 1824 (D) 1838. List-II: 1️⃣ First Anglo-Burmese War 2️⃣ First Anglo-Afghan War 3️⃣ First Anglo-Maratha War 4️⃣ Second Anglo-Mysore War. [1999]
questions.e: The First Anglo-Maratha War began in 1775. The Second Anglo-Mysore War started in 1780. The First Anglo-Burmese War began in 1824, and the First Anglo-Afghan War began in 1838.

questions.q: The last major extension of British Indian territory took place during the time of: [2000]
questions.e: Lord Dalhousie oversaw the last major expansion of British territory through the Doctrine of Lapse (annexing Jhansi, Satara, etc.) and on the pretext of misgovernance (annexing Awadh in 1856).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect? [2000]
o: Daman and Diu were separated from Goa by the 56th Amendment.
Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under French colonial rule till 1954.
Diu is an island in the Gulf of Khambhat.
questions.e: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under Portuguese colonial rule until 1954, not French rule. Goa attained statehood in 1987, and Diu is an island in the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.q: Who among the following Indian rulers established embassies in foreign countries on modern lines? [2001]
questions.e: Tipu Sultan was a forward-looking ruler who established embassies in France, Turkey, and Egypt to strengthen diplomatic ties and seek support against the British.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [2001]
o: India's first technicolour film-Jhansi ki Rani
India's first actress to win the Bharat Ratna-Meena Kumari
questions.e: Meena Kumari did not receive the Bharat Ratna. Other pairs are correct: 'Jhansi ki Rani' was the first technicolour film, and 'Taal' was the first insured film.

questions.q: Under the Permanent Settlement, 1793, the Zamindars were required to issue pattas to the farmers which were not issued by many of the Zamindars. The reason was: [2001]
o: the Zamindars were trusted by the farmers.
the farmers were not interested in getting pattas.
there was no official check upon the Zamindars.
it was the responsibility of the British government.
questions.e: Under the Permanent Settlement (1793), Zamindars often failed to issue 'pattas' (land deeds) to farmers because there was no effective official check or mechanism to ensure they complied with this requirement.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Arya Samaj was founded in 1835. 2️⃣ Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the appeal of Arya Samaj to the authority of Vedas in support of its social reform programme. 3️⃣ Under Keshab Chandra Sen, the Brahmo Samaj campaigned for women's education. 4️⃣ Vinoba Bhave founded the Sarvodya Samaj to work among refugees. Which of these statements are correct? [2001]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false (founded in 1875). Statement 2 is false as Lala Lajpat Rai did not oppose Arya Samaj's Vedic appeal. Keshab Chandra Sen did campaign for women's education, and Vinoba Bhave founded Sarvodya Samaj.

questions.q: Who amongst the following Englishmen, first translated Bhagavad-Gita into English? [2001]
questions.e: Charles Wilkins, a member of the Asiatic Society of Bengal founded by William Jones, was the first to translate the Bhagavad Gita into English in 1785 (often cited in context of the late 18th century).

questions.q: Which one of the following submitted in 1875 a petition to the House of Commons demanding India's direct representation in the British parliament? [2002]
questions.e: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, established in 1870 by M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi, submitted a petition to the House of Commons in 1875 for India's direct representation in the British Parliament.

questions.q: With which one of the following mountain tribes did the British first come into contact with after the grant of Diwani in the year 1765? [2002]
questions.e: After receiving the Diwani rights in 1765, the British first came into contact with the Khasi mountain tribe in the eastern frontier regions.

questions.q: Match List-I (Acts) with List-II (Provisions): (A) Charter Act, 1813 (B) Regulating Act (C) Act of 1858 (D) Pitt's India Act. List-II: 1️⃣ Set up a Board of Control 2️⃣ Company's trade monopoly ended 3️⃣ Power transferred to British Crown 4️⃣ Directors asked to present correspondence. [2002]
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly. The Regulating Act (1773) required directors to present documents. The Act of 1858 transferred power to the Crown. Pitt's India Act (1784) set up the Board of Control.

questions.q: Which one of the following Acts of British India strengthened the Viceroy's authority over his Executive Council by substituting "Portfolio" or departmental system for corporate functioning? [2002]
questions.e: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 introduced the portfolio system, allowing members of the Viceroy's Executive Council to take charge of specific departments, moving away from collective functioning.

questions.q: During the colonial period in India, what was the purpose of the Whitley Commission? [2003]
o: To develop a comprehensive scheme for Civil Services in India.
To report on existing conditions of labour and to make recommendations.
To review the fitness of India for further political reforms.
To draw up a plan for financial reforms for India.
questions.e: The Whitley Commission (Royal Commission on Labour in India), reporting in 1931, was established to investigate and report on the working conditions of labour in industrial undertakings and plantations.

questions.q: With reference to the entry of European powers into India, which one of the following statements is not correct? [2003]
o: The English opened their first factory in South India at Masulipatam.
In Eastern India, the English Company opened its first factory in Orissa in 1633.
Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied Madras in 1746.
questions.e: The Portuguese captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510, not 1499. Other statements regarding English and French factory/occupation locations and dates are correct.

questions.q: In India, among the following locations, the Dutch established their earliest factory at: [2003]
questions.e: The Dutch established their first factory at Masulipattanam (1605), but among the given options, Pulicat (1610) was their earliest established factory.

questions.q: The aim of education as stated by the Wood's Despatch of 1854 was: [2003]
o: the spread of western culture in India
the introduction of scientific research and rationalism in the traditional Indian education
the creation of employment opportunities for native Indians
the promotion of literacy among the people using English medium
questions.e: Wood's Despatch (1854), known as the Magna Carta of English education in India, aimed at introducing western knowledge, rationalism, and scientific research while recommending English for higher studies.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct? [2003]
o: Sawai Jai Singh of Amber had Euclid's Elements of Geometry translated into Sanskrit.
Ali Mardan Khan introduced the system of revenue farming in Bengal.
Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up modern foundries to manufacture cannons at Lahore.
Sultan Tipu of Mysore gave money for the construction of the idol of Goddess Sharda in the Shringeri temple.
questions.e: Farrukhsiyar introduced revenue farming in Bengal, not Ali Mardan Khan. Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Jai Singh, and Tipu Sultan's listed actions are historically accurate.

questions.q: Which one of the following provisions was not made in the Charter Act of 1833? [2003]
o: An Indian was to be appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General's Council.
All law-making powers to be conferred on Governor-General in Council.
The trading activities of the East India Company were to be abolished.
The designation of the supreme authority was to be changed as the Governor-General of India in Council.
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1833 provided for a Law Member (Macaulay was the first), but it did not stipulate that the member must be an Indian. Indians were not appointed to the Council at that time.

questions.q: With reference to colonial rule in India, what was sought by the Ilbert Bill in 1883? [2003]
o: To bring Indians and Europeans at par as far as the criminal jurisdiction of courts was concerned.
To encourage the native Indians to appear for civil service examinations by conducting them in India.
To allow native Indians to possess arms by amending the Arms Act.
To impose severe restrictions on the freedom of the native press.
questions.e: The Ilbert Bill (1883) sought to remove the disqualification of Indian magistrates from trying European subjects in criminal cases, aiming to bring Indian and European judges to par.

questions.q: In India, the first Bank of limited liability managed by Indians and founded in 1881 was: [2003]
questions.e: The Oudh Commercial Bank, established in 1881 in Faizabad, was the first bank of limited liability managed entirely by an Indian board. Punjab National Bank followed in 1895.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1️⃣ AD 1767-69: First Anglo-Maratha War 2️⃣ AD 1790-92: Third Mysore War 3️⃣ AD 1824-26: First Anglo-Burmese War 4️⃣ AD 1845-46: Second Sikh War. [2004]
questions.e: The Third Mysore War took place in 1790-92. The First Anglo-Burmese War was in 1824-26. The First Anglo-Maratha War was 1775-82 and the First Anglo-Sikh War was 1845-46.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [2004]
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act was passed by Lord Lytton in 1878 and repealed by Lord Ripon. Lord Curzon is associated with the Partition of Bengal.

questions.q: Consider the following Viceroys of India during the British rule: 1️⃣ Lord Curzon 2️⃣ Lord Chelmsford 3️⃣ Lord Hardinge 4️⃣ Lord Irwin. Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of their tenure? [2004]
questions.e: Lord Curzon (1899-1905), Lord Hardinge (1910-1916), Lord Chelmsford (1916-1921), and Lord Irwin (1926-1931).

questions.q: Consider the following princely States of the British rule in India: 1️⃣ Jhansi 2️⃣ Sambalpur 3️⃣ Satara. The correct chronological order in which they were annexed by the British is: [2004]
questions.e: Under the Doctrine of Lapse, Lord Dalhousie annexed Satara in 1848, Sambalpur in 1849, and Jhansi in 1854.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the Third Battle of Panipat, Ahmed Shah Abdali defeated Ibrahim Lodi. 2️⃣ Tipu Sultan was killed in the Third Anglo-Mysore War. 3️⃣ Mir Jafar entered in a conspiracy with the English for the defeat of Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah in the Battle of Plassey. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2004]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false: Abdali defeated the Marathas in 1761. Statement 2 is false: Tipu was killed in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799). Statement 3 is correct: Mir Jafar conspired with the British at Plassey.

questions.q: Which one of the following places did Kunwar Singh, a prominent leader of the Revolt of 1857 belong to? [2005]
questions.e: Kunwar Singh was a prominent leader of the 1857 revolt from Jagdispur, which is in the Bhojpur district of Bihar.

questions.q: Which one of the following territories was not affected by the Revolt of 1857? [2005]
questions.e: While Jhansi, Jagdishpur, and Lucknow were major centers of the 1857 revolt led by Laxmibai, Kunwar Singh, and Begum Hazrat Mahal respectively, Chittor remained largely unaffected.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar founded the Bethune School at Calcutta with the main aim of encouraging education for women. 2️⃣ Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was the first graduate of the Calcutta University. 3️⃣ Keshav Chandra Sen's campaign against Sati led to the enactment of a law to ban Sati by the Governor General. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2005]
questions.e: J.E.D. Bethune founded the school in 1849; Vidyasagar was closely associated. Bankim Chandra was one of the first graduates (1858). However, Raja Ram Mohan Roy (not Sen) led the campaign that prompted Bentinck to ban Sati in 1829.

questions.q: Who among the following repealed the Vernacular Press Act? [2005]
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act, introduced by Lord Lytton in 1878 to restrict the Indian press, was repealed by Lord Ripon in 1882.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct statement? [2005]
o: The Dutch defeated the Portuguese and built Fort Williams in the modern Kochi.
The modern Kochi was first a Dutch colony before the Portuguese took over.
The modern Kochi was a Dutch colony till India's independence.
The modern Kochi never became a part of a British colony.
questions.e: Kochi was first a Portuguese colony. The Dutch later defeated the Portuguese and built Fort Williams there. It eventually became part of the British colony.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Warren Hastings was the first Governor General who established a regular police force in India on the British pattern. 2️⃣ A Supreme Court was established at Calcutta by the Regulating Act, 1773. 3️⃣ The Indian Penal Code came into effect in the year 1860. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2005]
questions.e: Lord Cornwallis (not Hastings) established the regular police force. The Regulating Act (1773) did establish a Supreme Court at Calcutta, and the IPC came into effect in 1860.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the battles fought in India in the 18th Century? [2005]
o: Battle of Ambur-Battle of Buxar-Battle of Wandiwash-Battle of Plassey
Battle of Wandiwash-Battle of Buxar-Battle of Ambur-Battle of Plassey
Battle of Ambur-Battle of Plassey-Battle of Wandiwash-Battle of Buxar
Battle of Wandiwash-Battle of Plassey-Battle of Ambur-Battle of Buxar
questions.e: Battle of Ambur (1749), Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Wandiwash (1760), and Battle of Buxar (1764).

questions.q: Who among the following was a proponent of Fabianism as a movement? [2005]
questions.e: Annie Besant was a prominent proponent of Fabianism, a British socialist movement that advocated for gradual social reform rather than revolutionary change.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Charter Act, 1853 abolished East India Company monopoly of Indian trade. 2️⃣ Under the Government of India Act, 1858 the British Parliament abolished the rule of East India Company and undertook the responsibility of ruling India directly. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct? [2006]
questions.e: The Charter Act of 1813 (not 1853) abolished the Company's trade monopoly in India (except for tea and China trade). The 1858 Act correctly transferred rule to the British Crown.

questions.q: Which one of the following revolts was made famous by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in his novel 'Anand Math'? [2006]
questions.e: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel 'Anand Math' (1882) is set against the backdrop of the Sanyasi Rebellion of the late 18th century.

questions.q: With reference to the 'revolt of the year' (1857) who of the following was betrayed by 'friend' captured and put to death by the British? [2006]
questions.e: Tatya Tope was betrayed by his trusted friend, Man Singh, while hiding in the Paron forest. He was captured in April 1859 and subsequently executed.

questions.q: Who was the Governor-General of India during the Sepoy Mutiny? [2006]
questions.e: Lord Canning was the Governor-General during the 1857 Revolt (Sepoy Mutiny). He later became the first Viceroy of India under the 1858 Act.

questions.q: Who among the following started the newspaper Shome Prakash? [2007]
questions.e: The newspaper 'Shome Prakash' was started by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in 1858.

questions.q: The ruler of which one of the following States was removed from power by the British on the pretext of misgovernance? [2007]
questions.e: Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856 on the pretext of misgovernance, as the Doctrine of Lapse did not apply to Nawab Wajid Ali Shah who had heirs.

questions.q: The First Factory Act restricting the working hours of women and children and authorizing local government to make necessary rules was adopted during whose time? [2007]
questions.e: The First Factory Act was passed in 1881 during Lord Ripon's tenure to improve working conditions and fix hours for women and children.

questions.q: Who among the following Europeans were the last to come to pre-independence India as traders? [2007]
questions.e: The chronological order of arrival was: Portuguese (1498), Dutch (1602), English (1608/1599), and French (1664).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Robert Clive was the first Governor-General of Bengal. 2️⃣ William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2007]
questions.e: Warren Hastings (not Clive) was the first Governor-General of Bengal. William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833.

questions.q: Which one of the following was the first fort constructed by the British in India? [2007]
questions.e: Fort St George was built by the British in Madras in 1644. Fort William was built later (1781) in Calcutta. Fort St Angelo was built by the Portuguese.

questions.q: Who among the following wrote the book Bahubivah? [2007]
questions.e: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar wrote 'Bahubivah' (meaning polygamy) to protest against the social evil of men marrying multiple times.

questions.q: Match List-I (Author) with List-II (Work) and select the correct answer: (A) Bankimchandra (B) Dinabandhu Mitra (C) Premchand. List-II: 1️⃣ Shatranj ke Khilari 2️⃣ Debi Chaudhurani 3️⃣ Nil-Darpan 4️⃣ Chandrakanta. [2008]
questions.e: Bankim Chandra wrote 'Debi Chaudhurani'. Dinabandhu Mitra wrote 'Nil-Darpan'. Munshi Premchand wrote 'Shatranj ke Khilari'.

questions.q: In collaboration with David Hare and Alexander Duff, who of the following established Hindu College at Calcutta? [2009]
questions.e: Raja Rammohan Roy, in collaboration with David Hare and Alexander Duff, founded the Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The first telegraph line in India was laid between Kolkata and Diamond Harbour. 2️⃣ The first Export Processing Zone in India was set up in Kandla. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2009]
questions.e: The first electric telegraph line started between Kolkata and Diamond Harbour in 1850. The first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) was established in Kandla in 1965.

questions.q: Who among the following Governor Generals created the Covenanted Civil Service of India which later came to be known as the Indian Civil Service? [2010]
questions.e: Lord Cornwallis (1786–93) is known as the 'Father of Civil Services in India' for organizing and bringing into existence the Covenanted Civil Service.

questions.q: By a regulation in 1793, the District Collector was deprived of his judicial powers and made the collecting agent only. What was the reason for such a regulation? [2010]
o: Lord Cornwallis was alarmed at the extent of power concentrated in the District Collector.
Lord Cornwallis felt that judicial power should compulsorily be in the hands of Europeans.
Lord Cornwallis felt that the District Collector's efficiency of revenue collection would increase.
The judicial work demanded a deep knowledge of India and the Collector should be only a revenue collector.
questions.e: Under the Cornwallis Code of 1793, Cornwallis introduced the separation of powers. He felt that concentrating revenue and judicial powers in the Collector was undesirable and led to absolute power.

questions.q: What was the immediate reason for Ahmad Shah Abdali to invade India and fight the third battle of Panipat? [2010]
o: He wanted to annex the fertile plains of Punjab up to the borders of Delhi.
The frustrated governor of Jalandhar Adina Beg Khan invited him to invade Punjab.
He wanted to avenge the expulsion by Marathas of his viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore.
He wanted to punish Mughal administration for non-payment of revenues.
questions.e: The immediate cause of Abdali's fifth invasion (Oct 1759) was to avenge the expulsion of his son and viceroy, Timur Shah, from Lahore by the Marathas.

questions.q: With reference to Pondicherry (now Puducherry), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The first European power to occupy Pondicherry were the Portuguese. 2️⃣ The second European power to occupy Pondicherry were the French. 3️⃣ The English never occupied Pondicherry. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2010]
questions.e: The Portuguese established a factory in Pondicherry in the early 16th century. The Dutch (not French) were the second. The English also occupied it briefly in 1793 before returning it to the French in 1814.

questions.q: The tendency for increased litigation was visible after the introduction of the land settlement system of Lord Cornwallis in 1793. The reason for this is normally traced to which of the following provisions? [2011-I]
o: Making East India Company an overlord of Zamindars
Making Zamindar's position stronger Vis-Vis the Ryot
questions.e: Increased litigation was primarily due to the removal of Court Fees (making it easier to sue), the extension of the right to appeal, and the ability of ordinary people to sue government servants. None of the specific options a, b, or c fully capture this.

questions.q: Which amongst the following provided a common factor for tribal insurrection in India in the 19th century? [2011-I]
o: The complete disruption of the old agrarian order of the tribal communities.
Introduction of a new system of land revenue and taxation of tribal products.
Influence of foreign religious missionaries in tribal areas.
Rise of a large number of money lenders, traders and revenue farmers as middlemen in tribal areas.
questions.e: While revenue systems and middlemen played a role, the most comprehensive common factor was the total disruption of the traditional agrarian and social order of tribal communities by foreign interference.

questions.q: With reference to the period of colonial rule in India, "Home Charges" formed an important part of drain of wealth from India. Which of the following funds constituted "Home Charges"? 1️⃣ Funds used to support the India office in London. 2️⃣ Funds used to pay salaries and pensions of British personnel engaged in India. 3️⃣ Funds used for waging wars outside India by the British. [2011-I]
questions.e: Home Charges included the cost of the India Office in London, salaries/pensions of British officers, interest on debt, and costs associated with British troops serving India or waging related wars.

questions.q: What was the purpose with which Sir William Wedderburn and W.S. Caine had set up the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893? [2011-I]
o: To agitate for Indian political reforms in the House of Commons.
To campaign for the entry of Indians into the Imperial Judiciary.
To facilitate a discussion on India's Independence in the British Parliament.
To agitate for the entry of eminent Indians into the British Parliament.
questions.e: Wedderburn, as a liberal member of Parliament, established this committee to voice Indian grievances and agitate for political reforms within the House of Commons.

questions.q: With reference to Ryotwari Settlement, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The rent was paid directly by the peasants to the Government. 2️⃣ The Government gave Pattas to the Ryots. 3️⃣ The lands were surveyed and assessed before being taxed. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2012-I]
questions.e: In the Ryotwari system, the government dealt directly with the peasants (Ryots), issued them 'pattas' (title deeds), and the land was surveyed and assessed for revenue before taxation.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Brahmo Samaj? 1️⃣ It opposed idolatry. 2️⃣ It denied the need for a priestly class for interpreting the religious texts. 3️⃣ It popularized the doctrine that the Vedas are infallible. [2012-I]
questions.e: Brahmo Samaj opposed idolatry and the need for priests. However, it was the Arya Samaj (not Brahmo Samaj) that popularized the doctrine of Vedic infallibility.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Assessment of land revenue on the basis of nature of the soil and the quality of crops. 2️⃣ Use of mobile cannons in warfare. 3️⃣ Cultivation of tobacco and red chillies. Which of the above was/were introduced into India by the English? [2012-I]
questions.e: Revenue assessment based on soil was introduced by Raja Todarmal (Akbar's minister). Mobile cannons were used by Babur (1526). Tobacco was introduced by the Portuguese in the 16th/17th century.

questions.q: The Ilbert Bill controversy was related to the: [2013-I]
o: imposition of restrictions on newspapers and magazines published in Indian languages
imposition of certain restrictions to carry arms by the Indians
removal of disqualifications imposed on the Indian magistrates with regard to the trial of the Europeans
removal of a duty on imported cotton cloth
questions.e: The Ilbert Bill sought to allow Indian judges to try Europeans in criminal cases, a proposal that met with fierce resistance from the European community in India.

questions.q: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to: [2014-I]
o: solve the problem of minorities in India
give effect to the Independence Bill
enquire into the riots in East Bengal
delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan
questions.e: The Radcliffe Committee, led by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, was appointed to demarcate the international boundaries between the newly formed nations of India and Pakistan during Partition.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal made by Lord Curzon in 1905 lasted until: [2014-I]
o: the Partition of India in 1947 when East Bengal became East Pakistan
the First World War when Indian troops were needed by the British and the partition was ended
King George V abrogated Curzon's Act at the Royal Durbar in Delhi in 1911
Gandhiji launched his Civil Disobedience Movement
questions.e: The partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911 at the Delhi Durbar by King George V, at which time the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

questions.q: What was/were the object/objects of Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)? 1️⃣ To disclaim any intention to annex Indian States. 2️⃣ To place the Indian administration under the British Crown. 3️⃣ To regulate East India Company's trade with India. [2014-I]
questions.e: The 1858 Proclamation transferred the administration of India from the Company to the Crown and disclaimed further annexation of princely states. It did not aim to regulate the Company's trade as the Company's ruling power was ended.

questions.q: A community of people called Manganiyars is well-known for their: [2014-I]
o: pietra dura tradition in Central India
classical vocal music in South India
questions.e: Manganiyars are a tribal community from Rajasthan (North-West India) known for their rich and powerful musical traditions.

questions.q: The Ghadr (Ghadar) was a: [2014-I]
o: communist movement for India's freedom with headquarters at Tashkent
revolutionary association of Indians with headquarters at San Francisco
militant organization with headquarters at Berlin
questions.e: The Ghadar Party was a revolutionary association founded by Punjabi Indians in the US and Canada, with its headquarters (Yugantar Ashram) at San Francisco.

questions.q: With reference to Indian history, which of the following is/are the essential element/elements of the feudal system? 1️⃣ A very strong centralized political authority and a very weak provincial or local political authority. 2️⃣ Emergence of administrative structure based on control and possession of land. 3️⃣ Creation of lord-vassal relationship between the feudal lord and his overlord. [2015-I]
questions.e: Feudalism is characterized by a decentralized authority, administrative structures based on land possession, and the lord-vassal hierarchy. Statement 1 is incorrect because feudalism actually involves weak central authority.

questions.q: Who of the following was/were economic critic/critics of colonialism in India? 1️⃣ Dadabhai Naoroji 2️⃣ G. Subramania Iyer 3️⃣ R. C. Dutt. [2015-I]
questions.e: Dadabhai Naoroji, R.C. Dutt, and G. Subramania Iyer were among the early nationalists who developed a comprehensive economic critique of British colonialism (Drain Theory).

questions.q: The Government of India Act of 1919 clearly defined: [2015-I]
o: the powers of the Secretary of State for India and the Viceroy
the separation of power between the judiciary and the legislature
the jurisdiction of the central and provincial governments
questions.e: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919 Act) introduced Dyarchy and clearly demarcated the jurisdictions of the central and provincial governments through the division into central and provincial lists.

questions.q: Satya Shodhak Samaj organized: [2016-I]
o: a movement for upliftment of tribals in Bihar
questions.e: Satyashodhak Samaj was established by Jyotirao Phule in Maharashtra in 1873 with the aim of liberating lower castes and untouchables from exploitation.

questions.q: The Montague-Chelmsford Proposals were related to: [2016-I]
questions.e: The Montague-Chelmsford Report (1918) formed the basis of the Government of India Act 1919 and was focused on constitutional reforms and gradual introduction of self-governing institutions.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Calcutta Unitarian Committee 2️⃣ Tabernacle of New Dispensation 3️⃣ Indian Reform Association. Keshab Chandra Sen is associated with the establishment of which of the above? [2016-I]
questions.e: Keshab Chandra Sen established the 'New Dispensation' (Naba Bidhan) in 1881 and was part of the Indian Reform Association. The Calcutta Unitarian Committee was formed by Raja Rammohan Roy.

questions.q: What was the main reason for the split in the Indian National Congress at Surat in 1907? [2016-I]
o: Introduction of communalism into Indian politics by Lord Minto
Aurobindo Ghosh's inability to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress
Extremists' lack of faith in the capacity of the moderates to negotiate with the British Government
questions.e: The Surat Split occurred because the Extremists were dissatisfied with the Moderates' methods and their perceived lack of capacity to negotiate effectively with the British.

questions.q: The plan of Sir Stafford Cripps envisaged that after the Second World War: [2016-I]
o: India should be made a republic with the condition that she will join the Commonwealth
India should be partitioned into two before granting independence
India should be given Dominion status
India should be granted complete independence
questions.e: The Cripps Mission (1942) proposed that India would be given Dominion status and the right to frame its own constitution after the conclusion of World War II.

questions.q: With reference to cultural history of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Most of the Tyagaraja Kritis are devotional songs in praise of Lord Krishna. 2️⃣ Tyagaraja created several new ragas. 3️⃣ Annamacharya and Tyagaraja are contemporaries. 4️⃣ Annamacharya kirtanas are devotional songs in praise of Lord Venkateshwara. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2018-I]
questions.e: Tyagaraja (1767–1847) created many new ragas. Annamacharya (15th century) wrote in praise of Lord Venkateshwara. They were not contemporaries. Tyagaraja's kritis were primarily in praise of Lord Rama, not Krishna.

questions.q: The staple commodities of export by the English East India Company from Bengal in the middle of the 18th century were: [2018-I]
o: Copper, silver, gold, spices and tea
questions.e: During the 18th century, the English East India Company primarily exported fine textiles (cotton and silk), saltpetre (for gunpowder), and opium from Bengal.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley? [2018-I]
o: To secure a fixed income for the Company
To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
To maintain a large standing army at other's expense
To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
questions.e: The Subsidiary Alliance was designed to maintain troops at the expense of native rulers, ward off the French (Napoleon), and establish paramountcy. It was not primarily aimed at securing a "fixed income" for the Company.

questions.q: Economically, one of the results of the British rule in India in the 19th century was the: [2018-I]
o: growth in the number of Indian owned factories
rapid increase in the urban population
increase in the export of Indian handicrafts
questions.e: British policies led to the commercialization of agriculture (growing crops for the market rather than consumption), while handicrafts were ruined and industrial growth was restricted.

questions.q: Which among the following events happened earliest? [2018-I]
o: Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian to succeed in the Indian Civil Services Examination.
questions.e: Neeldarpan was written in 1858-59. Satyendranath Tagore cleared the ICS in 1863. Arya Samaj was founded in 1875. Anandmath was written in 1882.

questions.q: With reference to educational institutes during colonial rule in India, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Sanskrit College at Benaras: William Jones 2️⃣ Calcutta Madarsa: Warren Hastings 3️⃣ Fort William College: Arthur Wellesley. Which of the pairs given above is/are correct? [2018-I]
questions.e: Sanskrit College was founded by Jonathan Duncan. Calcutta Madarsa was founded by Warren Hastings. Fort William College was founded by Richard Wellesley (not Arthur, his brother).

questions.q: Regarding Wood's Dispatch, which of the following statements are true? 1️⃣ Grants-in-Aid system was introduced. 2️⃣ Establishment of universities was recommended. 3️⃣ English as a medium of instruction at all levels of education was recommended. [2018-I]
questions.e: Wood's Despatch (1854) introduced grants-in-aid and recommended university establishment. However, it recommended vernacular languages for primary/secondary education and English only for higher studies.

questions.q: Which of the following led to the introduction of English Education in India? 1️⃣ Charter Act of 1813 2️⃣ General Committee of Public Instruction, 1823 3️⃣ Orientalist and Anglicist Controversy. [2018-I]
questions.e: All three factors played a role: the 1813 Act sanctioned funds for education, the 1823 Committee managed it, and the Orientalist-Anglicist controversy was resolved in favor of the English medium.

questions.q: Who among the following were the founders of the "Hind Mazdoor Sabha" established in 1948? [2018-I]
o: Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta
B. Krishna Pillai, E.M.S. Namboodiripad and K.C. George
Jayaprakash Narayan, Deen Dayal Upadhyay and M.N. Roy
C.P. Ramaswamy lyer, K. Kamaraj and Veeresalingam Pantulu
questions.e: The Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1948) was founded with Ashok Mehta as General Secretary, along with leaders like T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta.

questions.q: Which one of the following foreign travellers elaborately discussed about diamonds and diamond mines of India? [2018-I]
questions.e: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier, a 17th-century French diamond merchant, visited India multiple times and wrote detailed accounts of its diamond mines and trading.

questions.q: Consider the following events: 1️⃣ First democratically elected communist party government in a State. 2️⃣ Imperial Bank of India renamed State Bank of India. 3️⃣ Air India nationalised. 4️⃣ Goa became part of independent India. The correct chronological sequence is: [2018-I]
questions.e: Air India was nationalized in 1953. Imperial Bank became SBI in 1955. The Communist government in Kerala was elected in 1957. Goa was liberated in 1961.

questions.q: With reference to land reforms in independent India, which one of the following statements is correct? [2019-I]
o: The ceiling laws were aimed at family holdings and not individual holdings.
Land reforms permitted no exemptions to the ceiling limits.
The major aim of land reforms was providing agriculture land to all the landless.
It resulted in cultivation of cash crops as a predominant form of cultivation.
questions.e: The primary goal of land reforms in independent India was social justice through the redistribution of land to the landless. Most early ceiling laws were initially based on individuals, not families, and many exemptions existed.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about 'the Charter Act of 1813': 1️⃣ It ended the trade monopoly of the EIC in India except for tea and China trade. 2️⃣ It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over Indian territories. 3️⃣ The revenues of India were now controlled by the British Parliament. Which are correct? [2019-I]
questions.e: The 1813 Act ended the monopoly (except tea/China) and asserted Crown sovereignty. However, parliamentary control over Indian revenues was established much later (fully after 1858).

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ All India Anti-Untouchability League: Mahatma Gandhi 2️⃣ All India Kisan Sabha: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati 3️⃣ Self Respect Movement: E.V. Ramaswami Naicker. Which are correctly matched? [2019-I]
questions.e: Gandhi founded the Anti-Untouchability League (1932). Sahajanand Saraswati was the first president of All India Kisan Sabha (1936). Naicker led the Self-Respect Movement.

questions.q: Indigo cultivation in India declined by the beginning of the 20th century because of: [2020-I]
o: Peasant resistance to the oppressive conduct of planters
National leaders' opposition to the cultivation of indigo
Its unprofitability in the world market because of new inventions
questions.e: The discovery of synthetic dyes in Germany at the end of the 19th century made natural indigo uncompetitive and unprofitable in the world market, leading to its decline.

questions.q: Wellesley established the Fort William College at Calcutta because: [2020-I]
o: He wanted to train British civilians for administrative purposes in India
He wanted to revive interest in oriental learning in India
He was asked by the Board of Directors at London to do so
He wanted to provide William Carey and his associates employment
questions.e: Lord Wellesley established Fort William College in 1800 to provide training in Indian languages and customs to young British civil servants newly arrived in India.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explain the impact of the Industrial Revolution on India during the first half of the nineteenth century? [2020-I]
o: Heavy duties were imposed on the imports of British manufactures.
Railway lines were laid in many parts of the country.
Machines were introduced in the Indian textile industry in large number.
questions.e: The Industrial Revolution in Britain led to the influx of cheap machine-made goods into India, which devastated traditional Indian handicraft industries during the early 19th century.

questions.q: The Vital-Vidhvansak, the first monthly journal to have the untouchable people as its target audience was published by: [2020-I]
questions.e: Gopal Baba Walangkar, a contemporary of Jyotiba Phule and leader of the Mahar movement, published 'Vital-Vidhvansak' in the 19th century to address the issues of untouchables.
